verneombud.title: The safety representative's role in mapping
verneombud.description: What is the safety representative entitled and obliged to do when the working environment is mapped? Access, involvement and raising it with management – with references to the law.
verneombud.h1: The safety representative's role in mapping the working environment
verneombud.lead: The safety representative shall see to it that the psychosocial working environment is safeguarded, and be consulted when measures are planned. That brings both rights and a role in the mapping itself. Here is what the law says, and what it means in practice.

blocks.text: What the law says
The safety representative shall safeguard the employees' interests in matters concerning the working environment.
blocks.cite: Working Environment Act § 6-2, first paragraph (our translation)

blocks.text: The section lists what the safety representative shall in particular see to. One of the points is that the employees' psychosocial working environment is safeguarded. The fourth paragraph says the safety representative shall be consulted during the planning and implementation of measures that matter for the working environment, including the organisation's systematic HSE work.

Section 1A-2 of the regulation on the performance of work also says the mapping and risk assessment of the psychosocial working environment shall be done together with the employees and their representatives. The safety representative is one of those representatives.
Must every organisation have a safety representative?

The main rule in section 6-1 is yes: a safety representative shall be elected in every organisation. Organisations with fewer than five employees may agree in writing on another arrangement. With more than ten employees, several safety representatives may be elected.
The safety representative's role, phase by phase

head: Phase
The safety representative's role
rows: Consulted on how the mapping is done, what it covers and how anonymity is secured
Can help employees know why they are getting the survey, and that it is safe to answer
Should see the same basis as management, not a summary afterwards
Consulted when measures are chosen and planned
Sees to it that the measures are actually carried out, and that the psychosocial working environment is safeguarded

blocks.text: Access in practice

The law uses the words «consulted» and «see to». It is hard to give good advice about something you have only seen a summary of. So the safety representative should have access to the same result as management – for the whole organisation and for the groups large enough to be shown.

Access does not mean access to individual answers. Anonymity applies to the safety representative as much as to management: nobody shall be able to see who answered what, and small groups shall not be shown to anyone.

blocks.title: In Orgpuls
blocks.text: The safety representative sees the same figures as the managing director, and follows the measures with their owner and deadline. The safety representative has access at no extra cost to the organisation.
How to raise it with management
Many safety representatives know the mapping should be done, but not how to raise it. Some advice:

items: **Start with questions, not demands.** «When did we last map the psychosocial working environment, and what happened to the findings?»
**Point to the rules.** Since 1 January 2026 the regulation says clearly that mapping shall be repeated regularly and documented.
**Propose a rhythm.** One main survey a year with short pulses in between is easier to achieve than a large project.
**Offer to take part.** A safety representative who helps explain the survey gives employees a reason to trust it.

blocks.text: On [the page for safety representatives](/verneombud) you will find a ready e-mail you can send to the managing director.
If the organisation has a working environment committee
The union representatives' role

Section 3-1, first paragraph, of the Working Environment Act says systematic HSE work shall be done together with the employees and their union representatives. Where the safety representative is responsible for the working environment, the union representatives represent the employees more broadly. Many organisations discuss a work environment survey with the union representatives before it goes out, treating it as a control measure under chapter 9 of the Act.
Situations you may meet
The result is poor for one department
Raise it as a finding, not a verdict. Ask what lies behind the figure, and let the department help choose the measures. Measures handed down without explanation rarely work.
Someone wants to see the figures for a small group

Stand firm. The limit on how small a group can be shown exists to protect employees, and it is why people dare to answer honestly. A group too small to be shown still counts in the figures for the whole.
Nothing happens after the survey
Ask about the measures: who owns them, and when are they due? Without an owner and a deadline, measures become intentions. The next survey is the best argument – it shows whether anything has moved.

Organisations where at least 30 people are regularly employed shall have a working environment committee (AMU). Between 10 and 30 employees, one shall be set up when one of the parties demands it. If there is an AMU, it is a natural place to raise the mapping and its follow-up.

plattform.lead: Orgpuls brings what the Working Environment Act requires of mapping into one steady rhythm. Each part can be used on its own, but the value is in how they connect: the survey becomes measures, and the next survey shows whether they worked.

blocks.text: Mapping

items.title: Baseline
items.text: Eleven psychosocial factors with three statements each, answered on a five-point scale. The wording builds on QPS Nordic and covers the factors named in section 4-3 of the Act and in the regulation. About four minutes per employee.

items.title: Pulse
items.text: Short surveys between baselines, only on the factors where a measure is running. The pulse is not a new mapping but a measurement of whether the measure works. Under a minute.

items.title: Your own questions
items.text: Up to five of your own questions per survey, for what is particular to you. They are reported separately and never enter the index.

items.title: Outside the index
items.text: A recommendation question, screening for offensive behaviour and for violence and threats – only as a count for the whole organisation – and an open field.

blocks.text: The survey is sent by e-mail or SMS, or shared as a link and a QR code. One reminder goes to those who have not answered, from the system and not the manager.
Results
The answers become an index from 0 to 100 per factor, with a risk band: 65 or above is low risk, 50–64 medium and below 50 high. The result can be read in several ways:

items: **Heatmap** – the factors against the departments, with the statements behind each figure
**Priority** – which factors matter most for whether people would recommend the workplace
**Segment profile, Compare and Development** – one department, two surveys, or the development over time

blocks.text: A department is shown once at least five have answered. When a department could be worked out from the others, one more is held back. Read more about [anonymity and security](/sikkerhet).
Comments and conversations

Employees can write a comment on a statement. Management can reply without knowing who wrote it, and the writer can read the reply and answer back through a private link. If a manager wants to talk directly, they can ask – and the employee alone decides whether to make themselves known, by writing an e-mail from their own e-mail.
Measures

The findings become measures on a board, from finding to effect. Each measure has an owner, a deadline and the factor it is meant to move, and ready suggestions are there to start from. **A measure cannot be closed before its effect is measured** – the next pulse must show whether the figure has moved.
Annual wheel and report

items.title: The annual wheel
items.text: You choose the rhythm once – from one baseline a year to a pulse every month – and the wheel plans the rounds itself. The safety representative and the union representatives are notified first, before the employees.

items.title: Report for inspection

sikkerhet.title: Security, privacy and anonymity | Orgpuls
sikkerhet.description: How Orgpuls keeps answers anonymous: no link to a person, at least five answers per group, data in the EU. What we store, and what we do not.
sikkerhet.h1: Anonymity that does not depend on anyone keeping a promise
sikkerhet.lead: Orgpuls promises that nobody can see who answered what. That promise is built into how the data is stored, not into a routine someone has to follow. Here is what that means in practice.

blocks.text: What we store, and what we do not

For each employee, the register holds name, e-mail and group, and a mobile number if you use SMS. The answer itself is stored in a table that **has no column that could hold a link to a person**. The row holds which round the answer belongs to, which group the person is in, and the hour it was submitted, rounded to the hour.

The invitation link is looked up by a cryptographic checksum when it is used. The invitation records that it has been used, so the reminder does not go to you – but never which answer it gave. There is no view, export or query that can say what a named person answered – not even for administrators – because the information does not exist.
Five answers, or a dash

No group is shown until at least five have answered. The limit is enforced by the database and cannot be lowered, only raised. When the figures for the other groups would reveal a hidden group, one more group is held back, so nobody can calculate their way there.
Comments and conversations

A comment is shown only when the group it comes from has enough answers, and the group never travels with the comment. The writer gets a private key to the conversation; the database stores only a checksum of it. If a manager wants to talk directly, they can ask – but only the employee can make themselves known, by writing from their own e-mail.
Legal basis

The legal basis is legal obligation, GDPR article 6(1)(c), with sections 3-1 and 4-3 of the Working Environment Act – not consent, because an employee cannot consent freely to their employer. The questions are designed to avoid health information, which an employer shall not collect. The screening for offensive behaviour and for violence and threats is reported only as a count.
Storage

items: The data is stored on servers in the EU (Frankfurt), under the GDPR
Answers are not shared with third parties, and no answers are used to train models
A single answer cannot be retrieved or deleted on its own, because it cannot be linked to a person (GDPR article 11)

blocks.text: Data processing agreement

The organisation is the controller, and Orgpuls AS is the processor. The data processing agreement under GDPR Article 28 is in Orgpuls under Settings, where the managing director reads and signs it, and can print or save it as PDF. The sub-processors are Supabase (database and sign-in, Frankfurt), Vercel (hosting, Frankfurt) and Brevo (e-mail and SMS).

blocks.text: Who is responsible

Orgpuls AS is the controller for the data described here: visits to the website, organisation signups, the newsletter, marketing and customer support. Send questions about privacy to [hjelp@orgpuls.no](mailto:hjelp@orgpuls.no).

blocks.title: Answers to employee surveys
blocks.text: When an organisation uses Orgpuls to survey its work environment, the organisation is the controller and Orgpuls AS the processor under a data processing agreement. Answers are stored with no link to the person who gave them. How that is built is described under [Security and privacy](/sikkerhet). Questions about a survey you take part in go to your employer.
When you visit the website

We keep our own statistics on the use of orgpuls.com, without cookies and without storing anything on your device. For each page view we store the page, the site you came from (the domain only), any campaign tags in the address (utm), an approximate location (country, region and city, derived from the IP address) and the network the IP address belongs to, cut to its first three of four parts (/24, or /48 for IPv6), and whether the visit came from a computer, a phone or a tablet, read from the browser's identification. The IP address itself and the browser's identification are not stored. Beyond this, they are used only to make a visit code that changes every day, so we can count visits within a day without being able to follow you from one day to the next.

If your browser asks not to be tracked (Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track), nothing is sent. The statistics are deleted after 13 months. In addition, Vercel, which hosts the website, measures page views and load times without cookies. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in understanding how the website is used, GDPR Article 6(1)(f).
When you register an organisation

We store your name, e-mail address, password (only as a cryptographic hash), the organisation's name, organisation number and number of employees, and information we fetch from the Brønnøysund Register Centre. We also store where the signup came from: the first page and any campaign tags from the same day's visit statistics, and your answer if you tell us how you heard of us. The legal basis is the agreement with the organisation, Article 6(1)(b), and our legitimate interest in knowing which channels work, point (f).
If you sign in with Google, we receive your name and e-mail address from Google. We never receive your password there.
When you try the demo

If you ask for a demo, we store the email address, whether you ticked the box for email from us, and a visitor code for the network you came from, made from the IP address with a key that changes every day. The IP address itself is not stored. The request is deleted after 30 days. We use it to send the sign-in link and to prevent misuse, such as many links to the same address. The basis is that you asked for the demo, Article 6(1)(b), and our legitimate interest in stopping misuse, point (f).

The demo is a copy of a fictional organisation that only you can access. It and your sign-in are deleted after 14 days without a sign-in, or as soon as you choose to create your own account. Once you have opened the link, we store the address as a contact marked «demo». We email you about Orgpuls only if you ticked the box, Article 6(1)(a), and you can unsubscribe in every email.
Newsletter and e-mail about Orgpuls

If you subscribe to the newsletter, we store your e-mail address, your name and organisation if given, the lists you chose and when you confirmed. The legal basis is your consent, Article 6(1)(a). We record whether a mailing was delivered, opened or clicked, to learn what is useful. You can unsubscribe with the link at the bottom of every e-mail, or choose your lists again. After you unsubscribe we keep only a cryptographic hash of the address, so that we do not send to it again.

We may send e-mail about Orgpuls to organisations' role addresses (such as post@), on the basis of legitimate interest. Personal addresses receive e-mail from us only with consent, or when you are already a customer and have not opted out. Every e-mail has an unsubscribe link. When we write to an organisation, we take its name, organisation number, industry and address from the Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities (Enhetsregisteret), and the general manager’s name from its public role information. We use the name only to address the organisation, at its own address. The basis is legitimate interest, Article 6(1)(f), and the information comes from a public source (Article 14). You can object at any time, see below.
When you contact us

If you write to us, through the form or by e-mail, we store your name, e-mail address and what you write, to answer and follow up. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in answering enquiries, or the agreement if you are a customer.
Cookies

We use only the cookies the service needs to work: signing in, your language choice, display choices in the app, and a short-lived cookie that remembers the organisation while you sign up with Google. None is used for statistics or advertising.
Who helps us

items: Supabase Inc. (USA): database, sign-in and background jobs. Data is stored in Frankfurt, Germany.
Vercel Inc. (USA): hosting of the website and the application, and the cookieless measurement of page views. Server functions run in Frankfurt.
Brevo SAS (France): sending e-mail and SMS, and recording delivery, opens and clicks on e-mail.
Google (Ireland): sign-in with Google, only if you choose it.

blocks.text: Suppliers outside the EEA are bound by the European Commission's standard contractual clauses for transfers. We do not sell personal data or share it with others for their marketing.
How long we keep data

items: Visit statistics: 13 months. The visit code changes every day.
The account and the organisation's data: for as long as the customer relationship lasts, and then as long as the Accounting Act requires for what is part of the accounts.
Newsletter: until you unsubscribe. After that, only the hash that prevents new mailings.
Support enquiries: as long as needed to follow up the case and the customer relationship.

blocks.text: Your rights

You can ask for access to, correction and erasure of data about you, ask us to restrict processing, object to processing based on legitimate interest, and receive data you have given us in a machine-readable format. Write to [hjelp@orgpuls.no](mailto:hjelp@orgpuls.no); we answer within 30 days. If you believe we process data in breach of the rules, you can complain to the Norwegian Data Protection Authority, [Datatilsynet](https://www.datatilsynet.no).

dpa.lead: This agreement governs how Orgpuls AS processes personal data on behalf of the organisation, under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Article 28. It follows the requirements the Norwegian Data Protection Authority (Datatilsynet) sets out for data processing agreements, and the structure of the European Commission's standard contractual clauses between controllers and processors (Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/915). This is a translation; the Norwegian version governs.

p: The organisation using Orgpuls is the controller. Orgpuls AS is the processor.
The organisation decides the purpose of the processing and which data is entered. Orgpuls processes the data only to provide the service.

Orgpuls processes personal data only to carry out the mapping of the psychosocial working environment under the Working Environment Act sections 3-1 and 4-3, as the organisation sets it up in the service: sending invitations and reminders, collecting anonymous answers, and showing results, measures and the report.

This agreement and the organisation's settings in Orgpuls are the documented instructions. Orgpuls shall inform the organisation at once if, in Orgpuls' view, an instruction infringes data protection law.
The data is not used for any other purpose, is not sold and is not shared with anyone other than the sub-processors in Annex 3.

Orgpuls is built to process as little personal data as possible. About employees, only name, e-mail address and, if the organisation enters it, mobile number are stored, together with their department. Answers are stored without any link to the person who gave them. Annex 1 describes the processing in full.
Everyone at Orgpuls with access to the personal data is bound by confidentiality. Access is given only to those who need it to operate and troubleshoot the service.
Orgpuls implements technical and organisational measures that ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, under GDPR Article 32. The measures are set out in Annex 2.

The organisation authorises the sub-processors in Annex 3. Orgpuls shall notify the organisation by e-mail at least 30 days before a sub-processor is added or replaced, and the organisation may object. If the parties cannot agree, the organisation may terminate the agreement before the change takes effect.
Orgpuls shall impose the same obligations on sub-processors as follow from this agreement, and is liable to the organisation for their performance.

The personal data is stored in the EEA, in Frankfurt, Germany. Some sub-processors are headquartered in the USA (Annex 3). Any transfer outside the EEA, including access from such countries, takes place only in accordance with GDPR Chapter V, for example on the basis of the European Commission's standard contractual clauses in the sub-processor's agreement.

Orgpuls assists the organisation, as far as possible, in meeting the data subjects' rights, such as access, rectification and erasure, and with the obligations in GDPR Articles 32 to 36: security, breach notification, data protection impact assessment and prior consultation.

The organisation can correct and delete employee data in Orgpuls itself. Anonymous answers cannot be linked to a person, and therefore cannot be retrieved or deleted for one particular person, under GDPR Article 11.

Orgpuls shall notify the organisation without undue delay, and no later than 36 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach. The notice shall describe what happened, which data and approximately how many data subjects are affected, the likely consequences and the measures taken, so that the organisation can notify Datatilsynet within 72 hours under GDPR Article 33.

Orgpuls makes available the information the organisation needs to demonstrate compliance with GDPR Article 28, and allows for audits, including inspections, by the organisation or an auditor it has mandated. Audits are announced at least 30 days in advance. The organisation bears the cost, unless the audit reveals material breaches of the agreement.

The agreement applies for as long as the organisation uses Orgpuls. When it ends, Orgpuls deletes the organisation's personal data within 30 days, unless the law requires it to be kept. Before then, the organisation can print or save its reports as PDF. Backups are deleted in the sub-processor's regular cycle.
Orgpuls may present a new version of the agreement in Orgpuls. The organisation is notified, and the new version applies once it is signed. Until then, the version last signed applies.
The agreement is governed by Norwegian law. In case of conflict, this agreement takes precedence over other agreements between the parties as regards the processing of personal data.

Purpose: mapping and follow-up of the psychosocial working environment under the Working Environment Act sections 3-1 and 4-3 and chapter 1A of the Regulations concerning the performance of work. The organisation's legal basis is legal obligation, GDPR Article 6(1)(c).
The data subjects are the employees the organisation invites to the mapping, and the organisation's users of Orgpuls: the managing director, department managers and safety representatives.
About employees, the following is stored:
ul: mobile number, only if the organisation enters it, for sending by SMS
which department the employee belongs to, and any role as safety representative, union representative or manager
for each survey: whether an invitation and a reminder were sent and whether the employee has answered, so that reminders go only to those who have not – never what the employee answered
the name of the person responsible for a measure, if the organisation chooses an employee as responsible

sections.h: Annex 1 – Answers, users and technical data
p: Answers are stored without name, e-mail address, invitation or any other link to the person who gave them: only which department the answer concerns and the hour it arrived. Results for a department are not shown until at least five have answered. Comments and replies in anonymous conversations are stored the same way. They may contain personal data if the writer includes it, and are never shown with a name.
About users, name, e-mail address, role and department are stored. Passwords are stored only as a cryptographic hash.

The questions are designed not to collect health data or other special categories of personal data, under GDPR Article 9 and the Working Environment Act section 9-3. The questions on offensive behaviour and violence are reported only as counts for the whole organisation.
The sub-processors record IP address and time in operational logs, used for operation and security. The statistics on use of the website use no cookies and do not identify visitors.
Retention: for as long as the agreement applies, unless the organisation deletes the data earlier or asks Orgpuls to do so.

ul: The data is stored in a database in Frankfurt, Germany, and is encrypted in transit and at rest.
Access control on every database table: a user sees only their own organisation, and only what their role allows.
The tables holding answers are closed to all users. Results are read only through functions that withhold departments with fewer than five answers.
The link an employee answers with is stored only as a SHA-256 hash. The time of an answer is stored rounded to the hour.
Sign-in with e-mail address and password. Passwords are stored as hashes.
Free text from employees is not written to logs or analytics tools.
Orgpuls' personnel access production data only when operation or troubleshooting requires it.
The database is changed only through versioned migration scripts, and the security rules are tested automatically on every change.
Supabase Inc. (USA): database, sign-in and background jobs. Data is stored in Frankfurt, Germany.
Vercel Inc. (USA): hosting of the website and the application. The server functions run in Frankfurt, Germany.
Brevo SAS (France): sending of e-mail and SMS.

faq.d: Can't find the answer? Write to us using the <link>contact form</link>. We reply personally, in Norwegian.

items.q: Can the manager see who answered what?
items.a: No. Responses are never linked to a name, email or IP. Groups are shown only once the threshold is reached — at least five responses — and that applies to administrators too.

items.q: Why not just one survey a year?
items.a: One survey shows how things stood at one point in time. It doesn't tell you whether the measures worked. The pulse measures only the factors you are working on, so you see the trend without asking about everything every time.

items.q: Won't people get tired of answering?
items.a: The pulse asks only about the factors you have open measures on, and a factor drops out once its measures are closed. What wears people out is answering without seeing anything happen — which is why everyone gets to see the measures.

items.q: Do we need an HR system?
items.a: No. Employees can be pasted in, uploaded as a CSV or added by hand.
You can switch off a factor, but not change the wording. That is what makes the figures comparable over time.

items.q: Does this cover all the requirements of the Working Environment Act?
items.a: Orgpuls covers the survey duty in § 3-1 c and the requirements for the psychosocial working environment in § 4-3, with documentation. Other HSE duties, such as incident reporting systems and sickness absence follow-up, are outside its scope.
